title: Find roots and intercepts from factorised form

source_reference.notes: Original Edexcel 4MA1 Higher-style item for the Year 10 quadratics MVP. Edexcel pivot metadata applied.

problem_text: The graph of y = (x - 2)(x + 4) crosses the x-axis at A and B. Find the x-coordinates of A and B, and find the y-intercept.
student_prompt: Show how you use the factorised form.
expected_answer: x-intercepts at x = 2 and x = -4; y-intercept = -8

error_category_mapping.diagnostic_sentence: For x - 2 = 0, the root is x = 2. The sign changes when solving the bracket equation.
The y-intercept happens when x = 0, not when y = 0.

hint_ladder.title: What do intercepts mean?
hint_ladder.prompt: An x-intercept happens when y is zero. A y-intercept happens when x is zero. Keep those two ideas separate.

hint_ladder.title: Pick a starting move
hint_ladder.prompt: Use the factorised form to find where the graph crosses the x-axis, then substitute zero for x to find the y-intercept.

hint_ladder.title: A common slip
hint_ladder.prompt: Check the signs of roots from brackets, then set x = 0 for the y-intercept.

hint_ladder.title: The general pattern
hint_ladder.prompt: For y = (x - r)(x - s), x-intercepts come from setting each bracket to zero; the y-intercept comes from substituting x = 0. Apply this pattern; do not copy an example.

common_errors: gives y values instead of x values
expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: The stuck point is reading roots from factorised form.
The stuck point is finding the y-intercept by substituting x = 0.

mark_scheme_notes: Award marks for both roots and y-intercept.
examiner_report_notes: Likely errors: reversed root signs and confusing x-intercepts with y-intercept.
metacognition_prompt: Before you start, what is the difference between x-intercepts and the y-intercept?
